Paragraph: In Chapter 6, Verses 5-6, Krishna states: 'One must elevate oneself by one's own mind, not degrade oneself. The mind is the friend of the conditioned soul, and his enemy as well. For him who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends; but for one who has failed to do so, his mind will remain the greatest enemy.'
Situation/Problem_Faced: Self-sabotaging thoughts, lack of internal discipline, and feeling victimized by one's own chaotic mental state.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna urges self-responsibility (Atma-uddhara), teaching that mental mastery transforms an intrusive, destructive mind into a supportive internal partner.
Outcome/Resolution: Developing cognitive control empowers individuals to cultivate self-compassion and mental resilience.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Emotional Regulation: Internal locus of control, Cognitive discipline

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Manas-Mitra vs. Manas-Satru (The mind as a friend versus an enemy)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Spiritual growth requires taking absolute ownership of one's mind, using spiritual discipline to turn inner turmoil into inner strength.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Highlights internal locus of control, self-efficacy, and countering cognitive distortions to prevent self-sabotage.
